checks.assessment: Short-range local ordering is distinguished from ordinary-crystal long-range translation-periodic order; absence of crystallinity is not described as complete local randomness. Ordinary-crystal qualification avoids claiming all crystals must be periodic.

Chemical composition SiO2 is correctly distinguished from quartz, its crystalline form. Formula unchanged. Figure81 two-dimensional network is explicitly a simplified structural comparison, not measured complete quartz/silica geometry. Six/five/seven ring classes remain source-defined.

Uniform statistically unoriented amorphous material without directional field/stress can show macroscopic isotropy; noncrystallinity alone does not guarantee every sample/property is isotropic. Glass example qualified; polymers may contain crystalline regions. Ordinary rock candy is crystalline sucrose, so the erroneous blanket source classification is explicitly corrected qualitatively without changing raw source.

Elastic/viscous response is qualified by material, temperature, stress and loading time relative to structural relaxation. Short-time solidlike response and long-time creep/flow are not generalized to all amorphous samples. Impact fracture is restricted to susceptible brittle samples. No claim of observable room-temperature window-glass flow; residence-time explanation remains a stated simplification, not one universal time.

Finite-observation low-temperature solidlike behavior and faster rearrangement on heating qualified. Glass transition is rate/time-dependent and not a sharp pure-crystal equilibrium melting point at fixed pressure. Crosslink/decomposition/crystallization alternatives not excluded by a blanket softening rule.
